title: 📖 Relative Clauses (यः...सः)
description: Learn to connect sentences using relative pronouns.

sections.title: 📖 What are Relative Clauses?
sections.content: Relative clauses connect two sentences using 'who', 'which', 'that', etc. In Sanskrit, we use यः (yaḥ) and सः (saḥ).

pronouns.example: यः अत्र अस्ति सः मित्रम्। (He who is here is a friend.)
या पठति सा छात्रा। (She who reads is a student.)
यत् फलम् तत् मधुरम्। (Which fruit is sweet.)
ये धावन्ति ते बालकाः। (Those who run are boys.)

complex_examples.translation: He who is a teacher goes.
I read the book which (is there).

questions.question: What does 'यः' mean?
questions.explanation: 'यः' (yaḥ) is the relative pronoun for masculine singular.

questions.question: How do you say 'He who reads knows' in Sanskrit?
questions.explanation: 'यः पठति सः जानाति।' uses the masculine singular form.

questions.question: How do you say 'She who reads is a student' in Sanskrit?
questions.explanation: 'या पठति सा छात्रा।' uses the feminine singular form.
